### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **214** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **154** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **154**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **99** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6833018f5db92e0b528e9dfd0a41995297a7984c` — the merge of head `ffbdd0fbe1dcea2d6b0aacf5e72b0c2a589c87ff` into base `0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6833018f5db92e0b528e9dfd0a41995297a7984c && git checkout 6833018f5db92e0b528e9dfd0a41995297a7984c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77 ffbdd0fbe1dcea2d6b0aacf5e72b0c2a589c87ff && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77 && git merge --no-ff ffbdd0fbe1dcea2d6b0aacf5e72b0c2a589c87ff

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0e78922ee07bda70879a49793159804fa6b41b77` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2be3fd45f4595b49ce7031091867d67e31350e13`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-materialization.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, .changeset/28534-installed-package-file-ref.md + packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts (`loadPackageFile` / `resolvePackagePath` TSDoc), packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts (`ConnectorBaseSchema` ... `MetadataProtectionFields`), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`ArtifactPackageSourceSchema`, `ArtifactPackageSchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts (`InstalledPackageSourceSchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts (`connector:` binding), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp`, `stampPackage`, the collection loop), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`installPackage`, `registerItem`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (`manifest` service `register`), packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts (`applyProtection`), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`resolveArtifactPackageEntries`), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (inline install, rehydrate), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts

Read at 2026-11-01T07:18Z, read-only: the diff `bca27ad3..2be3fd45` (5 files), card #28534 (body, triage 6554177417, claim 6554218344, dev report 6554765334 as claims to verify), PR #28587 body, and the cited code at `2be3fd45`. Nothing built or run. Check-runs on the head at read time: 36 success, 11 skipped, 10 still in progress (Build Core, Test Core shards 1, 2, 4 to 8, Type Check workspace and consumer gates), none failed.

### ① Derived judgments

- The contract (`connector-provider.ts` ~:320-350) promises a ref resolved "against the root of the stack/package that declared the entry". The runtime at `bca27ad3` handed every entry the host's root; the dev's base measurement of both members through the real install-local door is consistent with the code read. The premise holds.
- The fix classifies an entry as installed by one reading: `installedDeclaringPackageOf(entry, registry)` is `entry._packageId` looked up in the objectql package registry, installed iff `row.source === 'marketplace'`. I verified the writers of `source`: install-local writes `'marketplace'` at install (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1951`) and at rehydrate (`:1022`); `ObjectQL.registerApp` defaults `'code'` (`engine.ts:8782`) for the host stack, each member of an artifact's `packages[]` and every plugin manifest; `'authored'` is written only by `registry.installPackage(manifest, 'authored', ...)` from `protocol-package-install.ts:310`, `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:1697` and the `sys_packages` hydration (`service-package/src/index.ts:777`). The control-plane install (`POST /api/v1/cloud-connection/install`) only proxies to the cloud and registers nothing locally, so install-local is the only local door that writes `'marketplace'`. That half of the classification is sound.
- The other half is not: the stamp the classification reads, and the source the artifact entry may state, are both written by the installed package itself. Two reachable downgrades to the host's root, each through the card's own door, `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` with an inline manifest, by reading (not measured, read-only shape):
  - **(M1) A self-stamped `_packageId`.** `ConnectorBaseSchema` spreads `MetadataProtectionFields` (`connector.zod.ts:1055-1081`), so `_packageId` is a declared, optional key on a `connectors[]` entry and survives any parse. The managed install path registers the body as received (`normalizeBundle(inlineManifest)` → `convertPackageBodyForward` → `manifestService.register(converted, { source: 'marketplace' })` → `registerApp`); the collection loop registers each connector with `stampPackage(toRegister, ownerId, ownerVersion)` then `registerItem(..., ownerId)` (`engine.ts:9135`), and both stamp through `applyProtection`, which writes `_packageId` only while it is `undefined` (`protection.zod.ts:237`). Nothing refuses a body stamp that disagrees with `ownerId` for a connector (the ADR-0086 D3 refusal beside it covers `permissions` only). So an installed entry carrying `_packageId: 'com.host.showcase'` (a `'code'` row) or `_packageId: 'nobody'` (no row) is classified as the host's and handed `createPackageFileLoader(this.options.packageRoot)`: the measured cross-package read, one key away. The unit control "a stamp no row answers is the host's" pins the fail-open the spoof uses.
  - **(M2) An artifact entry stating `source: 'code'`.** install-local admits a body with `packages[]` (it reads `manifest.packages` itself at `:1667-1670`); the `manifest` service resolves entries through `resolveArtifactPackageEntries`, which keeps each entry's own `source` (`artifact-packages.ts:358`, `ArtifactPackageSourceSchema` admits `'code'` and `'marketplace'`, `stack.zod.ts:2010`), and registers with `source ?? options?.source` (`objectql/src/plugin.ts:944`): the entry's word wins over the door's `'marketplace'`. An installed bundle whose member states `source: 'code'` lands a `'code'` row, and every connector it declares reads the host's root. The spec's docblock reserves that statement for a control plane merging installs into the boot artifact; the install-local door does not withhold it.
- Fail-open on no registry / no row: no registry means no door could have written a row, which the code justifies. "A stamp no row answers = host" is the composed stack's residual owner (ADR-0130 D4) and is a real host case, but it is also what M1 exploits; it cannot stay a bare default once the stamp is the package's own word.
- Both members: `ConnectorProviderContext` has exactly two package-anchored members (`loadPackageFile`, `resolvePackagePath`); the built-in `openapi` factory dereferences only the first (`openapi-provider.ts:204`), `mcp` only the second (`mcp-provider.ts:351-352`), and neither reads `process.cwd()` itself; the only `process.cwd()` default is inside `resolveInsidePackageRoot` (`plugin.ts:315`), which an installed entry no longer reaches. `mcp-connector.ts:225` passes `transport.cwd` through, and `providerConfig.transport` carries no author-written `cwd` (the provider's own docblock). No third road found.
- Reconcile timing: `installPackage` writes the row before the collection loop registers any item (`registry.ts:6919-6931`, then `registerApp` step 2+), and `announceHotInstall` triggers `metadata:reloaded` with `{ changed: [...] }` only (`:3942`), so `captureReloadedConnectors` keeps no unstamped payload that could shadow the registry's stamped items. The materializer reads the registry object once per run but calls `getPackage` per entry, so the row is live. No ordering hole.
- Q1 (`'authored'`): reachable today, outside this card's ruling. `metadata-type-schemas.ts:272` binds `connector` to `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`, which carries `provider` / `providerConfig`, so a stored row with `providerConfig.spec: './x.json'` is storable through the metadata door; the post-boot reconcile reads stored rows through `readMetaItemsFromProtocol`, which stamps each with its `package_id` (`protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts:165`, an `'authored'` row or none) and both fall to the host's root. Also reachable with no package at all (an environment-authored connector), which is the same class on a hosted tenant. A finding to file, not a must-fix for this head.
- Q2 (every stdio `mcp` entry of an installed package refused): acceptable. The factory asks `resolvePackagePath('.')` unconditionally and the only alternative, no member at all, inherits the host's working directory (the measured reach by another road); the refusal and the docs name `http` as the road. Route B is not foreclosed.
- Message: the refusal is thrown before any resolution and interpolates only the entry name, the declaring package id and the author's own ref; no host absolute path can appear (pinned by `not.toContain(path.resolve(fixtureRoot))` in both unit cases). The `openapi` wrapper adds only its own prose. The cloud seat's finding 3 on #27293 holds here.
- Tests: the 6 unit cases and the 4 dogfood cases pin what the PR claims, including the host controls; the ablation the dev reports turns exactly the installed cases red. Nothing pins M1 or M2 because nothing in the design refuses them.
- Docs row and changeset: accurate for the mechanism as built (door names, `source: 'marketplace'`, `os build` remedy, `http` for MCP, host entries unchanged). The sentence "never resolved against the host's directory" overstates until M1 and M2 close.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-automation` patch, as declared. Behaviour narrows for one class of entry (an installed package's package-relative refs, and every stdio `mcp` entry of an installed package); no published schema or `packages/spec` member changes; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Boundary change: what an installed package's connector entry may read or launch on the host. The intended boundary (declaring package's root, never the host's) matches the contract text. The boundary as built is keyed on two inputs the installed package writes itself (M1, M2), so the installed package can opt out of it.
- Fail-open defaults: no registry (justified), a stamp with no row (unsafe while the stamp is the package's own).
- A hosted tenant never sees a host path in the refusal (verified).
- No `packages/spec` change; the claim's file surface is respected. Both remedies below sit outside `service-automation`; the claim says stop and report on that, so the seat widens the claim or routes them, rather than the dev deciding alone.

### ④ Design judgment

The change holds against the scenario it was accepted on (an honest installed manifest naming a host file or location) and against the contract's words. It does not hold against the adversary the card names ("an installed package must not be able to bind another package's files by guessing a path"), because the classification trusts the package's own `_packageId` and its own artifact-entry `source`. Must-fix and should-fix, one line each:

- **must-fix M1**: a connector (any collection item) registered under `ownerId` must not keep a body-carried `_packageId` that differs from `ownerId`: overwrite it, or refuse it the way `permissionSetOwnerRegistrationRefusal` refuses a permission set (`engine.ts:9120-9135`), and pin with an installed entry stamped `_packageId` of a `'code'` package being refused its ref.
- **must-fix M2**: an install-local install must register every `packages[]` member as `'marketplace'` whatever the entry states (refuse or override `source: 'code'` at the install-local door or make the door's `options.source` win in `objectql/src/plugin.ts:944` when the door states one), and pin it with a two-member inline bundle whose member states `source: 'code'`.
- **should-fix S1**: drop the bare "a stamp no row answers is the host's" default: answer host only for the residual owner id the artifact names (or no stamp), refuse every other stamp no row answers, and retitle the unit control accordingly.
- **should-fix S2**: file Q1 as a finding (class b): a stored or `'authored'` provider-bound connector row reads the host's root through the same two members, reachable through the metadata door bound to `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`.
- **should-fix S3**: the `installedDeclaringPackageOf` docblock should state what it trusts (the registering door's row) and what it does not (the item's stamp, the entry's stated source) once M1 and M2 make that true.
- **should-fix S4**: the dev's out-of-scope restart finding (installed connectors absent from `GET /automation/connectors` after rehydrate, inline entry included) is a real class a defect in a sibling lane; file it so it is not lost in a report comment.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-28534-installed-package-file-ref`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcVBKAFk1ntXSjvPt7U`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f8fa5255294b87be28f44a39a6162c2f72845a5e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/collection-item-owner-stamp.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-member-source.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-materialization.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-connector-package-ref.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, .changeset/28534-installed-package-file-ref.md, .changeset/28534-item-owner-stamp-refused.md, .changeset/28534-install-local-member-source.md + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`stampPackage`, `registerApp` owner key `manifest.id || manifest.name`, `registerMetadataCollections`, `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS`, seed `data[]`, `viewItems`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`registerItem`, `installPackage`), packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts (`applyProtection`), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts (`MetadataProtectionFields._packageId`), packages/spec/authorable-surface/integration.json, packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`artifactPackageId`, `resolveArtifactPackageEntries`), packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts (`_parseAndRegisterArtifact`, `registerArtifactBodyCollections`, the `manifest.register` of the metadata objects), packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts and packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts (how a boot feeds the two registrars), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (`POST /api/v1/packages`, the export `clean`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts, packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (ruling A, `CATEGORIES`, `findMigrationPrescription`), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the twelve level verdicts), AGENTS.md Post-Task 3, .claude/agents/os-dev.md (battery and declaration rules), the precedents eeb95f7 (objectql CHANGELOG) and .changeset/26711-view-write-door-unknown-key-refused.md

Read at 2026-11-01T08:59Z, read-only: the delta `2be3fd45..f8fa5255` (12 files, 3 commits), the prior record 6554878186, the claim amendment 6554888326, the dev's delta report 6555680458 as claims to verify, the PR body at the head, and the cited code at `f8fa5255`. Nothing built or run. Check-runs on the head at read time: 50 in all, 38 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, none in progress; every required context green. The dogfood matrix shards are among the skipped, so no dogfood file has run on this head in CI; the dogfood readings are the dev's local ones.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 as built.** `collectionItemOwnerStampRefusal` (engine.ts) refuses an item whose body carries a `_packageId` that is not `undefined` and not `ownerId`, in `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400 with `issues[]` at `_packageId`, before anything is filed; called in `registerMetadataCollections` (the manifest seam and every nested plugin run one body), on each seed `data[]` entry, on each `viewItems` body, and at the manifest service's residual door (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelItems`, both the container branch and the generic branch, after the name and permission-set judges). `null` and `''` fall to the refusal because `applyProtection` writes `_packageId` only while it is `undefined` (protection.zod.ts), so either would otherwise survive as an owner no row answers. Refuse-not-overwrite matches the two sibling refusals of the same loop and their recorded reason. Verified against the code and against the ten unit pins and the dogfood M1 case (422 `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` through the real door, no ledger entry, the host's file-ref entry still `ready`).
- **The exemption is sound.** `stampPackage` and `registry.registerItem` both stamp the CALLER's object in place (`applyProtection` "always mutates"), so an object registered once wears that registration's stamp for life; `noteRegistrationStamp` records that write in a process-wide `WeakMap` keyed by object identity, and the refusal exempts only `REGISTRATION_WRITTEN_STAMPS.get(item) === stamped`. For an install-door body to be exempt it would have to be the very object an earlier registration stamped. Every install door parses fresh: inline `req.json()` → `normalizeBundle` → `convertPackageBodyForward` → `asMarketplaceRegistration` → `register`; the managed path from the fetched payload; the rehydrate from the ledger file. A `structuredClone` or JSON round trip of a stamped object leaves the map and is refused (pinned: "a fresh copy wearing the same stamp is refused"), so the exemption only ever widens acceptance for the identical object, never for a value. The other registrar never meets it: `MetadataPlugin._parseAndRegisterArtifact` stamps in place with `artifactPackageId(body)` (= `id || name`, the same key `registerApp` uses) or the residual's `unclaimed.ownerId`, but files through the MetadataManager sink, not `registerApp`, and the boots that run both (`serve.ts`, `standalone-stack.ts`) hand the artifact door a file path and the `AppPlugin` its own object, so no stamped item object reaches `registerApp`. A `WeakMap` holds its keys weakly (no retention), is process-wide on purpose (the measured red was a module constant stamped by another engine in the same process), and its only history dependence is "an object a registration already stamped is accepted again", which no door can arrange. A narrower structural rule exists, stamping a copy instead of the caller's object, but it moves every consumer of the in-place stamp and is not owed on this head.
- **Door coverage.** install-local inline, managed and rehydrate → `manifest.register` → `registerApp`: covered. Code stacks, plugin manifests, the apps' `manifest.register(...)`: covered by the same loop. The residual door: covered. `POST /api/v1/packages`, the protocol's `installPackage` and the `sys_packages` hydration write an `'authored'` row through `registry.installPackage` and register no collection item (no `registerApp`/`registerItem` in those files), so M1 has nothing to judge there; stored rows reach the registry through `registerItem` with the row's `package_id` (`protocol-stored-overlay-reads.ts`), the S2 lane. `objects` is not in `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS`, so an object body's `_packageId` is not judged by this seam; an object carries no package-file ref, so nothing of this card rides on it. Note, not a finding.
- **M2 as built.** `asMarketplaceRegistration` restates every top-level `packages[]` entry whose `source` is stated and not `'marketplace'`, on a copy, by reference when nothing changes; applied at the two and only two `manifestService.register` calls of the file (install `:1987`, rehydrate `:1056`). `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` reads the top-level array only and never recurses, so the top-level restatement is complete. `objectql/src/plugin.ts:944` (`source ?? options?.source`) is byte-unchanged and `package-source-stamp.test.ts` is not in the diff: the boot artifact's entry-over-door precedence is untouched, as the claim amendment allowed. Pinned over a real engine (both rows `'marketplace'`, install and a pre-rule ledger entry) and through the real door (dogfood M2: 200, the member's file ref refused naming the member and "installed into this runtime", its inline sibling `ready`).
- **S1/S3 as built.** `nonHostDeclaringPackageOf`: no readers → host; no stamp → host; a row → `'marketplace'` is installed, any other source is host; no row → a residual owner a `'code'` door recorded is host, one a `'marketplace'` door recorded is installed; anything else (no record, or a non-string or empty stamp) is `unrecorded` and refused. `recordResidualOwner` is written by the manifest service with `options?.source ?? 'code'` before anything of the residual registers; only a door that states no source writes `'code'` (the boot's `manifest.register`), install-local always states `'marketplace'`, and a recorded `'marketplace'` never downgrades. A row is consulted before the residual record, so an installed package whose id collides with the host's residual owner reads installed, not host. I found no way for an installed package to get its id recorded as a `'code'` residual. The dev's acknowledged fail-closed side effect (a stored connector row stamped with a package no registration holds is now refused its refs) is the right direction and is in the S2 lane. The docblock states what it trusts and does not; accurate.
- **The exemption is applied unevenly.** `noteRegistrationStamp` follows `registerItem` at the collection loop and the seed loop, not at the `viewItems` site (engine.ts, after the new refusal there), although that site stamps the caller's object in place the same way. Harmless in production (no door re-registers a `viewItems` body under another id); a fixture shared across tests would be refused there and exempt one site up. Should-fix.
- **Legitimate producers of a differing body stamp — none found.** The package export strips every `_` key and `PROVENANCE_KEYS` (`packages.ts` `clean`); `os build`/`compile` stamps nothing (no `applyProtection` or `_packageId` write under `packages/cli/src`); the artifact loader stamps with the owner `registerApp` keys on and never hands that object to `registerApp`; the install ledger persists the body with stamps equal to the ids the rehydrate registers under (member → member id, residual → bundle id); the apps' module-constant manifests register under one fixed id each (equal stamp, or the map); seed bodies served by the package door are applied as rows, not re-registered; no stack under `examples/` or committed JSON carries `_packageId`. The pre-existing wrong-owner case (one object registered under A, then handed to B's registration) is kept as it was, which the dev notes; it is not reachable through a door.
- **Tests and ablations.** The unit, cloud-connection and service-automation pins and the two dogfood cases pin what the delta claims; the dev's M1 ablation at this head and M2 ablation at `7ea3d092` (file byte-identical at the head) turn exactly the new cases red, as reported. Not re-run here.
- **Docs row and changesets.** Accurate for the mechanism, with one wording nit: the docs row says "an entry carrying its own `_packageId` is refused at the install"; the refused case is a `_packageId` other than its package's — an equal stamp registers (pinned CONTROL).
